node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e places offering in Scope; node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5, node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5, node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 place promotional conditions in Scope. Failure therefore returns OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than the typed negative or compliant answer. This is a mismatch unless the assessment domain is expressly restricted to those conditions; that alternative remains unresolved.

The offer-level candidates combine an offer-wide promotional link with the existence of a non-discount gift component without expressly connecting that same component to the promotion. Mixed offers could be overclassified unless the supplied facts establish that connection.

The circular supports its SFC-authorised-fund context, but does not establish that paragraph 3.11 applies only to such funds. Conversely, broader product wording must remain bounded by the selected circular's actor and assessment scope.

Gift and discount classifications remain supplied judgments. Neither an additional return nor a guaranteed return automatically establishes a gift; a separate discount does not exempt another gift component. Passing this selected control does not establish compliance with disclosure, advertising or section 103 requirements.
The supplied text establishes no operative date interval. Temporal and conflict-handling conventions are implementation choices, not requirements proved by this source.
